sources.method: Found by the maintainers with FCEUmm RAM captures (scripted episodes, deterministic core) on a legitimately owned ROM (USA, Rev A / PRG1, iNES mapper 1; PRG0 is not covered). Second pass 2026-11-11: each former candidate was tested by perturbation, i.e. patching one byte of a saved state and replaying a script, with a stated expectation that could fail. xp: set to 6 and to 22, one slime kill later level rises to 2 and 3 exactly when xp reaches 7 and 23, and hp_max/mp_max follow (15 to 22, 22 to 24 and 0 to 5). hp: falls in fights (15 to 8), a herb raises it (5 to 15, capped at hp_max) and HEAL raises it (10 to 24, capped). mp: HEAL lowers it (5 to 1). item_bytes: 0xC0 is the herb count (a herb use takes it 3 to 2); 0xC1 to 0xC4 are the other inventory slots (two items per byte, a used item clears its slot in each of the four bytes). monster_id: 0 and 1 in the two kinds of fight seen (monster_hp 3 and 4); it holds a scratch value outside a fight, so read it only while monster_hp is above 0. monster_hp drops to 0 when the monster dies. menu_command: last chosen field command (1 status, 4 spell, 5 item, 7 take seen); cursor col and row follow the D-pad in the command window. command_window_tile is 0x64 while that window is drawn and 0xFF otherwise. spell_flags: with it at 0xFF the spell list opens and HEAL can be cast; at 0 the game refuses. Only that one effect was tested, not which bit is which spell. The XP table address came from a public disassembly as a lead; on our own ROM it reads as 30 strictly rising u16 values starting 0, 7, 23 and ending at 65535, and the level-ups above happen at its first two thresholds. map_id, player_x/y, gold, keys and message_window_tile come from the first capture pass: map_id changes only at stairs, doors and town entries, x/y change by one per step, gold rose 0 to 120 at a chest, 120 to 121 on a kill, fell 120 to 110 at a shop and 120 to 60 on game over, keys went 0 to 1 at the key chest and back at the door, and message_window_tile is 0x64 while the message window is drawn and 0xFF otherwise. The two ROM SHA-1s are the same Rev A ROM: the headerless (No-Intro) hash and the whole .nes file hash. CPU bus, internal RAM only, little-endian.
